title: How to Get Pre Approved for an Investment Property Loan: A Step-by-Step Guide
excerpt: Getting pre approved for an investment property loan is a critical first step before making offers on deals. This guide walks you through exactly what lenders look for and how to position yourself for approval.
author: AIWholesail Team
tags: how to get pre approved for an investment property loan
metaDescription: Learn how to get pre approved for an investment property loan with this step-by-step guide covering credit, income, down payments, and lender types.
metaKeywords: how to get pre approved for an investment property loan, investment property loan pre approval, rental property financing, investment property mortgage, real estate investor loan requirements

sections.content: Before you can make a competitive offer on your next rental, flip, or buy-and-hold property, you need one thing in your corner: pre approval. Knowing how to get pre approved for an investment property loan separates serious investors from window shoppers. Sellers and listing agents take you seriously. You know your budget. And you can move fast when the right deal shows up. This guide breaks down the entire process from start to finish. For a broader look at all your funding options, check out our [How to Finance Real Estate Investments: Complete Guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-financing) before diving in.
Investment Property Loans vs. Primary Residence Loans

First, understand that investment property loans are not the same as the mortgage you got on your home. Lenders view investment properties as higher risk because if times get tough, borrowers are more likely to stop paying a rental mortgage before they stop paying their personal home mortgage. That means stricter requirements across the board. You will typically need a higher credit score, a larger down payment, and proof of solid income. Interest rates on investment loans are also usually 0.5% to 1% higher than rates on owner-occupied homes. Knowing these differences upfront helps you avoid surprises during the approval process.
What Lenders Look at Before Approving You

Lenders evaluate several factors when deciding whether to pre approve you for an investment property loan. Understanding each one helps you prepare your application before you even contact a lender. Here is what they focus on most.
Credit Score Requirements

Most conventional lenders want to see a minimum credit score of 680 for investment properties. However, the best rates and terms go to borrowers with scores of 720 or higher. If your score is below 680, you are not out of options, but you will likely need to look at portfolio lenders or hard money lenders instead of conventional banks. Pull your credit report from all three bureaus before applying. Dispute any errors you find. Even a 20 to 30 point jump in your score can mean thousands of dollars saved over the life of the loan.
Debt-to-Income Ratio

Your debt-to-income ratio, or DTI, compares your monthly debt payments to your gross monthly income. For investment property loans, lenders typically want your DTI below 45%. Some will go up to 50% depending on other strong factors like a large down payment or significant cash reserves. Add up all your monthly obligations: your current mortgage or rent, car payments, student loans, credit card minimums, and any other loan payments. Divide that total by your gross monthly income. If you are at 42%, you are in decent shape. If you are at 55%, you need to pay down debt before applying.
Down Payment

Plan to put down at least 20% on an investment property. Many lenders require 25% for non-owner-occupied single-family homes or small multifamily properties. On a $250,000 rental property, that means bringing $50,000 to $62,500 to the table. Unlike primary residence loans, investment property loans rarely allow for low down payment programs. Having a larger down payment not only helps you get approved, it also lowers your monthly payment and improves your cash flow from day one.
Cash Reserves

Lenders want to see that you have money left over after closing. Most require at least three to six months of mortgage payments sitting in a liquid account. If you are buying a $200,000 rental with a $1,400 monthly payment, you need $4,200 to $8,400 in reserves beyond your down payment and closing costs. This shows the lender you can handle vacancies, repairs, or a slow rental month without defaulting on the loan.

Pro Tip: Keep your reserve funds in a separate savings account and avoid moving large sums in or out during the 60 days before applying. Lenders will review your last two to three bank statements, and unexplained deposits or withdrawals can raise red flags and delay your approval.
Step-by-Step: How to Get Pre Approved for an Investment Property Loan

items: Step 1: Check your credit report and score from all three bureaus. Fix any errors before applying.
Step 2: Calculate your DTI ratio. If it is above 45%, pay down debts before moving forward.
Step 3: Save for a 20-25% down payment plus closing costs (typically 2-5% of the loan amount).
Step 4: Build your cash reserves to cover at least 3-6 months of mortgage payments.
Step 5: Gather your documents — W-2s, tax returns (last 2 years), pay stubs, bank statements, and a list of current assets and liabilities.
Step 6: If you own rental properties already, compile your lease agreements and rental income history.
Step 7: Shop at least 3 lenders: a local bank or credit union, a mortgage broker, and an online lender.
Step 8: Submit your pre approval application. Avoid applying to more than 4-5 lenders at once to minimize credit score impact.
Step 9: Review your pre approval letter carefully — note the loan amount, interest rate, and any conditions you must meet before closing.
Step 10: Use your pre approval letter to make competitive offers with confidence.

sections.content: Which Type of Lender Should You Use?

Not all lenders are created equal for investment properties. Conventional banks and credit unions offer the best rates but have the strictest requirements. Portfolio lenders keep loans on their own books instead of selling them, so they have more flexibility with non-traditional borrowers. If you need to move fast on a distressed property, a [hard money loan](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/hard-money-loans-explained) might be your best short-term option — approval can happen in days rather than weeks, though you will pay higher rates. If you have equity in your primary home, a [HELOC](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/heloc-real-estate-investing) can serve as a flexible source of funding for smaller deals. And if you have retirement savings, it is worth learning about [Self-Directed IRA investing](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/self-directed-ira-real-estate) as a completely separate funding path that many investors overlook.

'Getting pre approved is not just about money. It is about proving to yourself and to sellers that you are a real buyer. The investor who closes fast wins the deal.' — Common wisdom among experienced real estate wholesalers and investors
How Rental Income Affects Your Pre Approval

If you already own rental properties, lenders will count a portion of your rental income toward your qualifying income. Most conventional lenders use 75% of your gross rental income to account for vacancies and expenses. For example, if a property rents for $2,000 per month, the lender counts $1,500 toward your income. If you are buying your first investment property, some lenders will factor in projected rental income from the subject property — but they will want a signed lease or a strong rental market analysis to back it up. Understanding how [analyzing real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) works will help you present a convincing rental income case to your lender.

Pro Tip: Use the free [Mortgage Calculator at aiwholesail.com/tools/mortgage-calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/mortgage-calculator) to run your numbers before meeting with a lender. Knowing your estimated monthly payment, cash flow, and break-even point ahead of time makes you look prepared and helps you ask the right questions.
Markets Where Pre Approval Gets You in the Game Fast

In competitive investor-friendly markets, having a pre approval letter in hand can be the difference between landing a deal and losing it. If you are investing in hot markets like [Dallas, TX](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/dallas-tx), [Atlanta, GA](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/atlanta-ga), or [Charlotte, NC](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/charlotte-nc), properties with strong cash flow potential move quickly. Sellers in these markets often receive multiple offers. A pre approval letter signals that you are financially ready and that the deal will close — which matters more to many sellers than the highest offer price. If you are newer to the investor side of real estate, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) explains how pre approval also helps you evaluate deals to assign or double-close without wasting time on properties outside your budget.
Common Mistakes to Avoid During the Pre Approval Process

items: Opening new credit cards or taking on new debt between pre approval and closing — this can tank your score or change your DTI.
Moving large sums of money between accounts without a clear paper trail.
Underestimating closing costs — budget 2-5% of the purchase price on top of your down payment.
Applying to too many lenders at once and triggering multiple hard credit pulls.
Forgetting to account for property taxes and insurance in your monthly payment estimates.
Not asking the lender about prepayment penalties or rate lock options upfront.

sections.content: One more thing worth knowing: a pre approval is not a guarantee of final loan approval. It is based on the financial information you provide upfront. Once you have a property under contract, the lender will do a full underwrite of both your financials and the property itself. Appraisals, title searches, and final verification of your income and assets must all check out before you hit the closing table.
